claims.explanation: E01 and evidence/proofs/calibration.md assert a universal permutation-calibration theorem under exchangeability. Finite threshold tests cannot express that mathematical theorem; the claim explicitly excludes a local finite-precision calibration interpretation.

E02 and evidence/proofs/fusion.md assert an unrestricted variational identity with integrability and absolute-continuity assumptions. Numerical equivalence on a finite RunPair would not establish that identity or preserve its posterior domain.

E01/E02 and evidence/proofs/fusion.md give a conditional mathematical implication for every finite positive invariant normalizer. Testing a few row permutations would narrow this universal statement to one implementation and finite samples.

E03 and evidence/proofs/power.md retain author-stated sufficient-power bounds with boundedness, fixed-prior, permutation and reciprocal-moment hypotheses. The catalog has no relation encoding the theorem or its proof obligations.

E03/E08 concern the divergence term in a sufficient condition, not measured monotonic power. Figure 7 does not measure posterior divergence, so a monotonic relation on its rejection proportions would substitute a different claim.

E02/E09 assert the absence of an additional multiplicity-calibration stage in the algorithm. Figure 8 runtime comparisons do not establish that structural assertion, and the claim explicitly disclaims universal wall-clock superiority.

E04 and Figure 1 provide whole-method comparisons, while C07 is a bandwidth-scale mechanism hypothesis requiring all other components held fixed. Comparing MMD-FUSE and MMD-Median rejection proportions would not isolate that mechanism.

Figure 1, Galaxy: sample size, retains the image-specific MMD-D and MMD-FUSE rows at all five sample sizes. The statement says can exceed, so consistency with min_pass=1 expresses existence over the full named sweep rather than universal dominance or inferential significance. The panel pin excludes synthetic MMD-D and the AutoML variant.

C09 and evidence/figures/figure7.md explicitly leave the inferential noninferiority margin, starting collection/expansion acceptance rule, paired outcomes and simultaneous uncertainty procedure unfrozen. Choosing a tolerance from the observed sweep would invent the missing acceptance criterion.

Table 1 reports aggregate rejection proportions but C10's falsification criterion requires source-denominator reconciliation and a prespecified uncertainty comparison to the null level. Neither inferred binomial counts from rounded decimals nor a pairwise comparison among the 13 methods expresses the full assertion.

E10/E11 combine an aggregate reproduction with a symbolic mismatch between executed and paper exponents. evidence/results/local_run.md supplies the numerical match, but no catalog relation checks the symbolic non-equivalence conjunct documented in evidence/source_conflicts.md.

E12 and evidence/admission/frozen-protocol.json define the finite treatment mean band [0.13,0.23], reference band, label-permutation maximum 0.1 and minimum reference-to-control drop 0.05. The invariant excludes the reference from the treatment mean and retains the control gate. Only batches for the registered two-treatment seed or row-order families are admissible; no generic family is attached because its schema cannot pin the original exact seeds and row-manifest identities. Existing admission results are not supplied as fresh RunBatch cases in this study, so this declaration needs protocol-aligned cases and has zero declared generator pairings.
